text.p: These are the leading stories in Serbian and Montenegrin press on Friday. Reuters has not verified them nor does it vouch for their accuracy.
- S E R B I A -
POLITIKA
- Yugoslav President Zoran Lilic says the non-existant problem of Kosovo was fabricated for some other purpose.
- Yugoslav business delegation visiting New York agrees with president of London Club to hold new meeting by the end of June.
- Austrian political-economic delegation visiting Yugoslavia shows readiness to promote bilateral relations.

- Yugoslav-Russian joint venture company Yugo-Ros gas will build gas pipeline Pojate-Nis-Dimitrovgra and networks in central and eastern Serbia and Kosovo, deputy general manager of Serbian petrol Industry NIS Milan Mladenovic said.
- Yugoslav-British firm with majority British capital Novolab was opened in Belgrade Thursday. It will supply the Yugoslav market with laboratory equipment.
- Mt.Kopaonik is covered with 20 cm of snow and the temperature is one degree Celsius below zero.
- Serbian information minister Radmila Milentijevic expects the new information law to be adopted by end of June.
NASA BORBA
- Serbian President Slsobodan Milosevic will not run for a third presidential mandate, said his wife Mira Markovic in Thessalonika Thursday.
- Thousands of pensioners protest in Belgrade Thursday over late pensions.
- Yugoslavia will not extradite indicted war criminals to the Hague but will try them in the country if there are grounds, says spokesman of the ruling Socialist Party of Serbia Ivica Dacic.
- Former Yugoslav Intrerior Minister Vukasin Jokanovic to be appointed new Federal Public Prosecutor.

- Slovenia considers unacceptable memorandum on succession of ex-Yugoslavia proposed by international mediator Sir Arthur Watts because it does not explicitely say former Balkan federation has five successor states.
VECERNJE NOVOSTI
- Iron lady returns to Belgrade, commentary on fothcoming visit of U.S. Secretary of State Madeleine Albright.
POLITIKA EKSPRES
- Serbian government preparing short term measures to resolve some education problems to ensure succcessful end of school year, says Education minister Jovo Todorovic.
GRADJANIN

- Slovenia ready to drop suits filed against Yugoslavia if Belgrade agrees to divide embassy buildings abroad among all former Yugoslav states, the paper quotes Slovenian succession team head Miran Mejak as saying in an interview to Ljubljana paper.
- M O N T E N E G R O -
POBJEDA
- Slovaks interested in financing Montenegrin-Slovak bank that will finance future joint ventures. Slovak state delegation led by finance minister Karol Czesnik visiting Montenegro.
- After 49 days of strike 669 workers of timber company Velimir Jakic from Pljevlja agreed to resume production. Management will pay outstanding wages for January, February and March.
MONITOR

- The final clash in the ruling Democratic Party of Socialists (DPS) will be on July 11 when the main board elects its presidential candidate. If president Momir Bulatovic is not nominated he will be politically anihilated, if he is, DPS will split into two parties.
- Newly formed committee for control of the security service will be made up of members of all parties five from the opposition and six from the DPS.

- Yugoslav information minister announces opening of new federal television station JRT including Montenegro. The director of the new TV will probably be Milorad Vucelic, close ally of Serbian president Slobodan Milosevic. -- Belgrade newsroom +381 11 222 4305
